recipes.name: Baking Mix Blackberry Cobbler
ingredients_raw: 1 cup all-purpose baking mix (such as Bisquick®)

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease a 9x9-inch baking dish.

Whisk baking mix, milk, 1/3 cup sugar, and oil together in a bowl until no large lumps remain. Pour into the prepared baking dish. Whisk water and 2/3 cup sugar in a clean bowl until mixed. Gently fold in berries until evenly coated; spread berry mixture over baking mix batter.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden on top and fruit is bubbling, about 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Baking Mix Blackberry Cobbler
raw_recipe.description: This Bisquick blackberry cobbler is super easy to make with fresh or frozen blackberries and baking mix for a comforting, crowd-pleasing dessert.

review.reviewBody: For requiring so few ingredients, this cobbler was awesome! I added some cinnamon to the blackberries, and cut the water back to 3/4 cup. Served warm with vanilla ice cream. Thanks, AshleyElaine, for the recipe. I'll definitely be making this again!

I made this for my husband's company picnic. I ended up doubling the recipe. I took other people's suggestions and added lemon juice and cinnamon to the blackberries. I didn't add the 1 cup of water since the freshly picked blackberries produced their own juices when I add the sugar to it. Followed the cake exactly as indicated. I put parchment paper on the bottom of the baking pan and put the blackberries on top of the paper and the batter on top the blackberries. After they were done baking and let it cool for about an hour, I flipped the pan over on a big plate and garnished it with more fresh blackberries. It was pretty sweet but I like it that way to counter act some of the tartness of the blackberries.

Followed to the the letter, but made one deviation. Instead of oil, I used applesauce - two healthy tsp. Kept the 1/3 cup of sugar, but reduced the berry sugar by a half. Came out very good. Baked it in a 9 inch glass pie pan in my toaster oven - 35 min. Very very good. 
The berries were thawed from a frozen state, but the cooked up beautifully.

I am going to make this the second time - just like I did the first -- here are my modifications:
1. Used a 13 x 8 pan. 
2. Had closer to 3 cups of blueberries and 3 apricots
3. Added about 1/3 more of the bisquick, sugar, milk to the cobbler portion
4. Added about 1 tbs cinnamon and 1 tbs lemon juice and 1 tsp pure vanilla extract. 
put in the oven for 40 minutes or so.

I was happy to find this recipe to use what I had on hand in a mountain cabin. I used blueberries. I made this at high altitude (not my usual baking location). I was hesitant to add so much sugar water with the berries, so I used half of the sugar water and it turned out fine. We pressed the berries into the batter and that worked out too. I checked every 10 minutes because of the altitude. Served with French vanilla ice cream. Delicious!

Made it for second time today. Modified again making two cobblers at once. One peach and one strawberry with dabs of sweetened cream cheese on top. I added tablespoon of almond extract and sprinkled in cinnamon to the batter along with tiny dabs of butter to top of batter. Towards last ten minutes of baking I sprinkle brown sugar for a crispy sweet bite.
This was a huge hit! Are used granulated Stevia instead of sugar. The brand of Stevia that I used indicated using 1/2 of the amount of sugar called for, which I did. No one was the wiser!!
I doubled the batch to include rasberrys so 2 cups blackberries and 2 cups raspberries
Do NOT use all of the water or it will be a soupy mess. Only use half that the recipe calls for. Sub in melted butter for the oil also

I picked some wild black raspberries today and had to make a cobbler with it. I doubled the crust and put it on top like another reviewer did bc I was hoping for a crunchier crust. I also took another reviewers advice and added about a tblsp of cornstarch as a thickening agent (to the water, sugar and berry mix). Despite it not having a bit of a more solid bite the cobbler was delicious and I would make it again, with the revisions I just mentioned. I might even use shortening instead of oil, I'll keep you posted. For now, this will be my go to for a berry cobbler.

Wow, quick to put together and hubby &I ate 3/4's of it. The only thing I changed was I used 2 apples chopped small to equal 2 cups and 1tsp cinnamon along with only 1l3 cup sugar mixed with water. So good we couldn't wait to cool it down.

I was worried about how much water was being used so I used one egg in with the bisquick batter! It was perfect. Made the batter more cake-like, which helped the absorption of any extra liquid without changing the taste of the cobbler. Next time I'll do just as instructions say 😉 GREAT RECIPE

The blackberries at the market did not look very fresh, so I picked up a pint of fresh blueberries. This is a very unusual recipe. The way it’s written is telling you to make the batter and pour into the dish. Then you whisk 1 cup water and 2/3 cup sugar, “gently fold in berries” and “spread” the berry mixture over the batter. Basically, what you have is a bowl of water with berries floating on the top. The berries are never incorporated into the batter, and you end up with a layer of somewhat gummy/syrupy cake topped with gooey berries. It was too sweet for us, that could be personal taste, but this not cook up like any cobbler I’ve ever made. We ate it, but I didn’t save leftovers. Won’t be making this again.
Watery
Just finished this blackberry cobbler. Haven't tried it yet, But it sure looks good! Love this recipe. Didn't have to add lemon or cornstarch. Just like my grandma made.

I just made this. I used chopped thawed strawberries instead. Also added 2 tsp of vanilla to the bisquick mix. Make sure and spread the bisquick mix all the way to the corners. Mine didn't spread out by itself. Very delicious recipe!
I'm not a baker and had doubts about the liquid, but it turned out great
Excellent recipe!

Like another reviewer said, this recipe gets 5 stars for the ease but 3 stars for the taste. Both my husband and I felt that it's like eating blackberry hotcakes/muffins. This will be a good breakfast recipe, but not as dessert.
Easy and delicious. will be my go-to recipe for this now. perfect for a small family. We have 3 in our family.
